text:
For the 2050s under a middle-of-the-road emissions scenario, the best match for the farm's future climate is Whitman County, Washington. This location is a strong match, and all 8 climate models agree. Sigma measures how different a place's climate today is from the farm's future climate in units of the farm's normal year-to-year swings, where lower means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Regarding crop rotations, 1 out of 5 matching areas uses the field's current rotation, which is a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, and winter wheat. The rotations used at the matching places include a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, and winter wheat; winter wheat to fallow; and winter wheat to spring wheat to fallow.

Looking at hazards compared to the best match, the field has 18 hot days above 32 degrees Celsius per year compared to 28 at the match. The frost-free season is 150 days at the field and 186 days at the match. For afternoon ground temperature in June, the field sits at 31.9 degrees Celsius while the match is 31.2 degrees Celsius. For July and August afternoon ground temperature, which is mostly after harvest, the field is at 37.4 degrees Celsius and the match is 42.1 degrees Celsius. The driest-month soil water in September is 16.6 percent for the field and 17.2 percent for the match. 

Overall, temperatures rise across all periods while precipitation changes vary by season. These results are based on candidates from 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometers using the Cropland Data Layer.
